parts.text: Which claim builds the prime factorisation of $84$ correctly?

options.text: The prime factorisation of $84$ is $2 \times 2 \times 3$ from $12$ alone.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: The prime factors of 12 and of 7 combine to give the prime factorisation of the product 84.

teacher.key_rationale: Prime factorisation of a product joins the prime factorisations of its factors: 12=2×2×3 and 7=7, so 84=2×2×3×7. Leaving 12×7 treats composite factors as the prime factorisation. Using only 12's primes omits the factor 7.
